Facebook Link Chef Nancy Silverton debuted her Pacific Palisades restaurant Spacca Tutto on Thursday, October 15, as an opening the enclave needs. After the Palisades Fire tore through the coastal community in January 2025 , the neighborhood lost homes, residents, and nearly a dozen restaurants , along with damage to its centerpiece Palisades Village. Palisades Village owner Rick Caruso recently reopened his retail and restaurant property, where Silverton will debut a menu inspired by sister restaurant Chi Spacca in Hollywood, a modern Italian steakhouse. As you travel on the Palisades–Malibu–Santa Monica stretch of Pacific Coast Highway, you can still see extensive impacts from the Palisades Fire. Entire properties sit ravaged and empty, some with tattered blue tarps and wild brush overgrowth, while others are peppered with construction crews deep in the rebuilding process. Many of Pacific Palisades’ wildfire survivors remain scattered throughout the Southland. But now they can return to Palisades Village, which is still under construction. Some restaurants have opened in recent months, including Porta Via , Alphabet Bar and Grill , and, as of Thursday, Spacca Tutto. Caruso, a major fan of Chi Spacca, invited Silverton to create Spacca Tutto’s menu. “The first person I thought of was Nancy,” Caruso told Eater in 2025. “She’s an L.A. original. Jeremy Fox’s beloved Santa Monica restaurant, Birdie G’s , will resurrect at Fairmont Century Plaza after closing at the end of 2025. Named after Fox’s daughter Birdie and grandmother Gladys, the restaurant will reopen on October 26, serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner with a mix of original favorites, such as the Pickle Chick, and new dishes, including a Rancho Gordo bean–based poached egg ribollita. When Fox first spoke with Fairmont Century Plaza about Birdie’s G’s in June 2025, it was supposed to be the restaurant’s second location. Legendary Los Angeles diner Swingers opens in the former Silver Lake All Day Baby space on Tuesday, October 20. Smash burger restaurant Heavy Handed previously occupied the storefront, opening on the corner in March 2025 before closing just a year later in spring 2026. Swingers will initially open with takeout only, with the dining room slated to open fully in December. Swingers first opened on Beverly Boulevard in 1993 , slinging steaming cups of coffee and French toast until the early hours of the morning. The iconic Googie cafe inspired the 1996 movie Swingers (although the film was shot at the former 101 Coffee Shop) and appeared in other Hollywood productions, including Knocked Up and Insecure. The diner has long held a special place in Angelenos’ hearts, conjuring memories of late-night breakfasts in plaid booths with dishes splayed across gleaming orange tables. Swinger’s announced it would close permanently in April 2020 due to impacts of the pandemic , but reopened in November 2020 under new owner Stephanie Wilson , the former general manager who has been with the restaurant since 2010 in different roles. Wilson tells Eater she long believed Swingers would do well in the Silver Lake area and had been looking for the right home; when the former All Day Baby space became available, it just felt right, she says. Andrea Jernmark Matthew Kang is a correspondent for Eater. Previously, he was the lead editor of Eater’s Southern California/Southwest region. He has covered dining, restaurants, food culture, and nightlife in Los Angeles since 2008. Sign up for his weekly newsletter, Kangtown . In our Dining Reports, we share a firsthand perspective of a recent restaurant visit, covering everything from the vibe to must-get dishes. See more in the Eater app. Download the app In the year of the California-French bistro , chef Marcus Jernmark’s Marée has emerged as a top contender, hovering over sister tasting menu restaurant Lielle, which earned a Michelin star mere months after first opening in February. Marée strives to be more casual (the final bill may beg to differ, however), with an approachable wine list — no cocktails here — and polished French dishes like mussels “gratin,” grilled Caledonian prawn cocktail, and grilled pork chop dressed in herbaceous Cafe de Paris sauce. The fairly spartan room, which used to be beloved Peruvian restaurant Picca and then the fancy Michelin-starred Manzke, has soaring ceilings that contribute to an increasingly rowdy scene as the evening progresses. Warmth comes from the weathered hand-drawn menus on the wall mirrors, as well as the open kitchen that churns out grilled hamburgers au poivre — about 25 per night, to create just the right amount of fervor around them. Marée may be the freshest bistro in Los Angeles, but it already feels lived in. What to order Cute, creamy mussels au “gratin” are the ideal starter, slurped up like warm oysters and amplified by a basket of plush baguette slices, anchovies, baby radishes, and softened butter. A proper bistro meal needs some bite-building interaction to get you in the mood. Grilled Caledonian shrimp “cocktail” comes with an adorable metal bird lemon squeezer to dab on acid to every bite. Facebook Link Matilda’s , a new powerhouse bakery that mostly sells more than 3,000 pastries every week, opened in early October in a restored 1940s administrative building at the Santa Monica Airport. With so much early interest, the bakery has already experienced 45-minute lines with customers clamoring to secure croissants, sausage rolls, Danishes, cookies, sandwiches, baguettes, and sample Matilda’s butter tasting menu, which encompasses eight different tastes and styles. Owner and restaurateur Sean Martin took over the building in 2022 and recruited former social marketing campaign maker and founding baker Francois Pied. Pied tells Eater he’s been overwhelmed by the response. “I am still processing it, to be honest,” he says. “I was not expecting this level of commitment from people to stand in line.” On October 12, the shop issued an Instagram apology and thanked those who stood in line for pastries its first few weeks. Pied, who was born in France, tapped Abel Pulsifer (Brooklyn’s Radio Bakery ) as lead baker; the duo met at Bub and Grandma’s before working on Matilda’s, which is named after Martin’s daughter. Matilda starts by sourcing its flour from Hayden Flour Mills, which specializes in reviving ancient and forgotten grains. The duo slow-ferments their pastry dough for at least 18 hours, with a four-day process for butter, ham and cheese, almond, or pain au chocolat croissants. The menu also offers chocolate chip cookies, sausage rolls that have been flying off the shelves, and honey butter or traditional brioche. On August 19, Nixta Taqueria and Lao’d Bar will collaborate on a two-part, six-course dinner that gives diners a chance to explore Mexican and Laotian cooking back-to-back, through bold flavors, shared traditions, and personal storytelling. The evening will open with Chef Edgar Rico’s signature masa-driven cooking, including duck carnitas tacos and Denver steak aguachile. Chef Bob Somsith will follow with dishes inspired by the flavors of Laos, from shrimp ceviche with fried stuffed shrimp head to a fish laab tostada. And expect a delightful collaborative dessert showcasing the best of both restaurants. “I’ve always believed food is one of the best ways to tell your story,” says Bob Somsith at Lao’d Bar. “I’m excited to share the kitchen with Edgar and explore the common threads between Lao and Mexican cuisine. Different histories, different flavors, but the same belief that food has the power to bring people together.” Chef Rico from Nixta agrees. “Even though our cultures are oceans apart, they share so many of the same values: hospitality, honoring those who came before us, and creating flavor bombs that stop you in your tracks.” Tickets are selling out fast, so if you’re in Austin on August 19, get yours today . And download the Eater app to hear about more great events like this. See you at the Bang Bang. Under glittering chandeliers, pros like Ben Shelton, Tommy Paul, Leylah Fernandez, and Maria Sakkari played showcase matches as spectators sipped from Champagne flutes. The sports-tourism market was estimated to be worth $1.16 trillion in 2025 and now makes up about 10 percent of the tourism economy itself. It's the perfect amalgam of travelers' growing pursuits of wellness, mental stimulation, and once-in-a-lifetime experiences on their journeys. Create your trip here North America Chevron United States Chevron New York Places to Stay My Favorite Airbnb: A Hudson Valley Retreat With a Creekside Hot Tub and Sauna Between its storybook interiors and proximity to small-town shops, farm stands, and cider orchards, this group-friendly stay is one of my favorite upstate discoveries. By Jessica Chapel October 17, 2026 Courtesy of Airbnb Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story Getting 12 people to agree on a weekend away is an exercise in logistics. Someone wants to hike ; someone else would rather browse antique shops; a few people are already asking what’s for dinner. My ideal group getaway? One that leaves room for all of it, with a house you're excited to return to in between excursions. On a recent October weekend , my friends and I—a total of six couples—found that combination at Schoonmaker Retreat , tucked in the quaint Hudson Valley hamlet of High Falls. As a lifelong New Yorker , I’ve made plenty of trips to the Catskills and Hudson Valley, but High Falls, Rosendale, and Accord were towns I hadn’t yet gotten to know. Rosendale had been on my radar thanks to the introduction of Six Bells Countryside Inn , a delightfully whimsical, British-inspired hotel, and the surrounding area seemed ripe for a fall weekend of vintage shopping , cider tasting, and lots of leaf-peeping . We lucked into a real Goldilocks window, with timing just right for trees to stand ablaze with reds, yellows, and the last bits of green. The weather was crisp, but still sunny enough to sit outside for hours, from long orchard lunches to cozy s’more nights. The Schoonmaker Retreat is in Ulster County, which straddles the towns of Rosendale and Marbletown. With two separate houses, a rushing creek running through the grounds, and a sauna and a cedar barrel hot tub beside the water, the sprawling estate gave our group a place to gather (or rather, frolic) between outings. We arrived on a Friday, trickling in at different times before tackling the first order of business: choosing bedrooms . The property has two historic buildings—the main, more contemporary Schoonmaker House and the slightly smaller, rustic-chic, and creekside Coach House. The latter is the property’s original base, used as a fort used for Mr. Schoonmaker himself during the Revolutionary War. The Story Behind the Façade Restoring the hotel’s historic exterior will require more than just throwing up the scaffolding and calling in a team. By Timothy Latterner October 16, 2026 Getty Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story Of the 700+ hotels in New York City , The Plaza Hotel stands apart. Surrounded by skyscrapers, the stout, eighteen-story building at the corner of 59th Street and 5th Avenue, just south of Central Park , is more of an icon in the cityscape than any of its super-tall neighbors could hope to be. It hosted The Beatles just before their breakthrough performance on The Ed Sullivan Show , welcomed F. Scott and Zelda Fitzgerald, inspired the eponymous Neil Simon play Plaza Suite , acted as a backdrop in Home Alone 2, and was the home of the fictional Eloise , the little girl who roamed its elegant halls. Now, nearly 120 years after it first opened, it’s shutting its doors—at least for a few years. The Plaza's façade and the interior of the hotel are registered landmarks, recognized by both the national and city government. Richard Mandelkorn Starting in 2027, the Plaza Hotel will embark on a four-year-long renovation of its marble façade. First designed by Henry Janeway Hardenbergh in 1907, the hotel’s base and lower levels are crafted from rusticated marble, with the upper levels being made from a polished, smooth marble exterior. Rusticated marble deteriorates more quickly when exposed to the elements, and can often need to be repaired and restored within twenty years. Coincidentally, the 2027 renovation comes just 19 years after the last major renovation to the hotel in 2008. Restoring the hotel’s façade will require more than just throwing up the scaffolding and calling in a team. The façade and the interior of the hotel are recognized as registered landmarks both nationally and by the city. The Landmarks Preservation Commission is working closely with the hotel to help with the restoration efforts and preserve the architectural beauty of the building. By Jessica Chapel and Caitlin Morton October 15, 2026 Getty Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story If there’s one thing that can make me fall in love with winter, it’s the thought of wandering around a European city with snow under my boots , twinkling lights overhead, and somewhere cozy to duck into when the temperature dips too low. I’m always chasing snow, whether that means clipping into my snowboard for a few days on a mountain or venturing somewhere that feels especially magical in the colder months—and Europe in particular has a way of making winter feel like something to celebrate. From Austria to Norway , winter transforms medieval streets into living storybooks beneath a fresh dusting of snow. Christmas markets turn historic squares into glittering wonderlands, and cozy cafés become an excellent excuse to linger over a rich hot chocolate or mulled wine while the world passes by. It's like stepping straight into your own magical snow globe. The appeal of these 15 cities extends well beyond December. Throughout the chilly season, head to Alpine towns framed by dramatic mountain peaks, indulge your adventurous side on a lesser-known arctic escape, or visit a grand European capital that feels more intimate after the summer crowds have dispersed. If you do visit after the holiday rush, you'll likely find more room to explore at your own pace. Consider this your invitation to trade the winter blues for European enchantment—snow-dusted rooftops, candlelit dinners, northern lights, and all. — Jessica Chapel Pinterest Unsplash Luxembourg City, Luxembourg Best for: Fairytale fortifications and festive Christmas markets Luxembourg City makes a compelling case for a winter getaway, with its UNESCO -listed Old Town, centuries-old fortifications, and dramatic valleys that feel even more magical in the colder months. From late November through early January, the annual Winterlights festival transforms the capital with Christmas markets, illuminated streets, live performances, and an ice-skating rink. Browse the chalets for local specialties like Gromperekichelcher (Luxembourgish potato fritters), before warming up with hot chocolate or mulled wine. We loved poring over the results to find out what’s sticking with readers and spinning the data into a snapshot of the current moment in travel. Ahead: your manual for planning that next adventure. View the complete list of Readers’ Choice Award winners here . Mexico City is a metropolis that cares deeply about design. That means you’ll want to pack with an eye toward color, structure, and pattern, especially when checking in to this landmark Four Seasons property , which is fresh off an expansive reimagining by Mexican architecture firm Huber. Interior details are a celebration of the handmade: Ceramics, textiles, and hand-blown glass are sourced from local artisans in craft centers like Guadalajara and Michoacán ; red marble flooring in the rooms comes from Durango. And while Mexico City street style is some of the world’s best, the bar for dressing well here is set inside the lobby, where the staff wear uniforms by homegrown designer Kris Goyri. Christian Horan Save to wishlist Save to wishlist Christian Horan Save to wishlist Save to wishlist Christian Horan Save to wishlist Save to wishlist Christian Horan Save to wishlist Save to wishlist Chevron Chevron Four Seasons Hotel Mexico City Readers' Choice Readers' Choice Awards 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2026 Even though it’s set on busy Paseo de la Reforma, this name-brand luxury hotel delivers tranquil, boutique charms. Rooms are set around an interior courtyard, and you’re just a short distance from Chapultepec Park, offering respite from the hustle and bustle of Mexico City. Add to that all the other Four Seasons hallmarks—insanely comfortable beds, high-quality service, and wellness amenities like a pool, gym, and spa—and you’re guaranteed a memorable experience. Locations In new cities we look for demand drivers and the ability to achieve appropriate rates with a market that can demonstrate a balance of business and leisure demand. We look for access to a major airport with international inbound flights. The cities should have a gap in the market for, or the ability to support a top tier hotel. Properties We have a preference for buildings with personality and character. Historic buildings should be rich in stories and the ability to be upgraded for modern luxury. We also consider new buildings, however these must have exceptional features and stunning public spaces. Submit 2026® PC Studio 2025 Brooklyn, NY Office Role Interior Design Scope Renovation: Studio, Material Library, Library, Kitchen and Meeting Rooms Partners Contractor: Whitenight Contracting Photographer: Chris Mottalini Partners: Roll & Hill, Nordic Knots, Tretiak Works Project Narrative The overall studio is anchored by a primary open space flanked by smaller symmetrical “parlors.” The open space is defined by its pure utility, a series of massive metal work tables customized for the needs of the team through wire cages and metallic interventions. These parlors define the various sequences of the design process from a study/library where the team explores conceptual research to a robust material library, both an archive of prototypes and working resources. Interior partitions echo a classic wood and glass language while the separations allow for exploration of color and architectural reference within the rooms. items.title: High Peaks Residence
items.text: High Peaks Residence Post Company Post Company Close Information Studio Contact Approach Community Press & Accolades Catalogue Branding Collection Post Company Catalogue Branding Collection Information Studio Contact Approach Community Press & Accolades Newsletter Please enter a valid email address You're in. Submit 2026® High Peaks Residence 2026 Adirondacks, NY Residential Role Interior Design Scope Renovation and New Construction: Private Residence Partners Architect: Phinney Design Group Kitchen Design: deVOL Photography: Chris Mottalini Project Narrative The house sits deep in the Adirondacks, fifteen miles from the nearest town, built in the 1890s for a Manhattan lawyer who wanted somewhere to disappear. It had been renovated many times since — sometimes carefully, sometimes not. When our clients bought it, they brought a different ambition: not to restore it to any particular moment in its history, but to make it feel as though it had always been exactly this way. The program was generous in scale and social in spirit. Across the main house and carriage house, the property needed to accommodate twenty guests — five bedroom suites, two bunkrooms, a commercial kitchen, and enough variety of space that people could be together and have completely different experiences. The design responded to that multiplicity: rooms of different scales and moods, each with its own character, all held within the same framework of restraint. Interiors were stripped of the expected Adirondack register — the dark wood, the antlers, the rustic theatrics. Instead, limewash walls in Farrow & Ball Schoolhouse White, wide oak floors, coffered ceilings painted out to give the rooms room to breathe. The test was whether, from the inside, you could guess anything about the outside. We were glad when the answer was no. Furniture was assembled across eras and geographies — Pierre Chapo stools, Swedish shelving, Welsh Stick chairs reinterpreted by Greg Mitchell, antique Heriz rugs, Henning Kjærnulf armchairs, a French Provincial oak sideboard anchoring the stair hall. Nothing from a single period or place. Objects chosen for what they do in a room, not what they signal about it. The house is not complete until it is filled with people. That was the brief, more or less, and the rooms were designed to make it true. Instagram 45 Main St. Ste 844, Brooklyn NY 11201 Newsletter Please enter a valid email address You're in. items.title: Baby Grand
items.text: Baby Grand Post Company Post Company Close Information Studio Contact Approach Community Press & Accolades Catalogue Branding Collection Post Company Catalogue Branding Collection Information Studio Contact Approach Community Press & Accolades Newsletter Please enter a valid email address You're in. Submit 2026® Baby Grand 2026 Coronado, CA Hotel, Food & Beverage Role Interior Design, Branding & Identity Scope Renovation: 31 Room Hotel, F&B Outlets (Night Hawk, Fallen Empire), Lobby, Cafe, Pool, Outdoor Spaces Partners Owner: Consortium Holdings Architects: Tucker Sadler Photography: Ethan Jones Project Narrative The Baby Grand transforms a former asphalt lot into a 31-room hotel that reads like a place reclaimed by time. Mature plantings, gas-lit torches and weathered statuary suggest a property slowly overtaken by nature, while mosaic floors, mirrored walls and iridescent clamshell beds build a world that feels assembled over years rather than months. The result is theatrical without being staged, a hotel meant to be discovered rather than checked into. The lobby marks the shift from Coronado's shoreline into something older and stranger, lined with tapestries modeled on Pompeiian wall paintings beneath a fabric ceiling and central chandelier. Concealed within it is Fallen Empire, a hidden oyster and champagne bar with mirrored walls, brass booths in red mohair and a mosaic floor depicting life underwater. Guest rooms carry the same instinct for accumulation: custom clamshell beds, tropical Schumacher wallpaper, high-gloss wood ceilings and oxblood trim, furnished with vintage artwork as if gathered over time. Bathrooms take up nearly half of each room's footprint, with mosaic tile, marble consoles and clawfoot tubs turning bathing into its own small theater. Our renovation foregrounds the historic character of the original building, while affirming the contemporary relevance of the new Fedora with a space that is both elevated and firmly grounded in its context. items.text: MOLLIE Aspen Post Company Post Company Close Information Studio Contact Approach Community Press & Accolades Catalogue Branding Collection Post Company Catalogue Branding Collection Information Studio Contact Approach Community Press & Accolades Newsletter Please enter a valid email address You're in. Submit 2026® MOLLIE 2024 Aspen, CO Hotel, Food & Beverage Role Interior Design, Branding & Identity Scope New Construction: Lobby, Restaurant & Bar, Cafe, Retail, Guest Rooms, Rooftop Bar Partners Owner / Client: HayMax Capital Architect: CCY Architects Food & Beverage: Gin & Luck Contractor: SHAW Construction Project Narrative MOLLIE is based in the early history of Aspen in more than its name. The building is inspired by Bauhaus artist and architect Herbert Bayer, who in 1946, was avidly recruited by Walter Paepcke and his wife Elizabeth to help implement their vision of Aspen as a special community organized around art and culture. Bayers influence on Aspen is evident today in his architectural designs for numerous prominent institutions in the city. MOLLIE’s essence is an homage to the work of Bayer. MOLLIE's interiors are subtly inspired by the Aspen tradition of being firmly grounded while gazing abroad. The property holds a quiet confidence and commitment to a reduction of excess with interiors that thoughtfully utilize native materials from Aspen and the wider Western region, accentuated with natural woods, earthen ceramics, and hand-dyed textiles. items.title: The Rounds at Scribner's
items.text: The Rounds at Scribner's Post Company Post Company Close Information Studio Contact Approach Community Press & Accolades Catalogue Branding Collection Post Company Catalogue Branding Collection Information Studio Contact Approach Community Press & Accolades Newsletter Please enter a valid email address You're in. Submit 2026® The Rounds at Scribner's 2024 Hunter, NY Hotel, Food & Beverage Role Building Design, Interior Design Scope New Construction: 12 Cabins, Central Lodge Amenity Building & Bar Partners Client: Escape Hospitality Engineer: Taconic Engineering Contractor: Bast Hatfield Photography: Chris Mottalini Project Narrative Building upon the whimsical and communal Scribner’s Lodge (2016), the Round’s were imagined to offer a new more intimate, residential experience. A short hike up the hill from the Lodge, the Round’s were designed to provide an immersive experience and holistic appreciation for the surrounding landscape and beauty of the area. Seeking inspiration from the hut systems of Europe and the hand-hewn shingled traditions of the Catskills, the collective team sought to define a new building typology; one that would be in service of reflection and enjoyment of one’s surroundings. The guest buildings revolve around a centralized amenity lodge; an inviting locus for friends and new acquaintances alike to meet and reconvene throughout their stay. At the heart of each room, a central oculus allows one to experience the shifting light and shadows through the day. The team developed a circular strategy to the buildings as a device to frame specific vantage points while maintaining privacy. Each Round has 12 sides, where each facet holds a different program for daily routines, for example, a daybed, a wet bar, or stove. The structures are clad entirely in shingles, speaking to local historic vernaculars while the interiors adopt the use of knotty pine throughout the spaces. At the center of the suites, a sunken circular sofa references Scribner’s more recent mid-century history-this time dressed in a more subdued and minimalist fashion. The baths echo the same geometry where a round marble sink aligns with the axis of the room. The main lodge features a bar for small parties and lounge spaces for larger gatherings. The design team tapped notable furniture designers from across the Hudson Valley and North East to build heirloom quality pieces, with the intention to highlight the incredible craft in the area. items.title: Modelos
items.text: Modelos Inicio Bio Clientes Contacto Inicio Bio Clientes Contacto Retrato La fotografía de moda va más allá de capturar una imagen; es contar una historia, evocar una emoción y dar vida a una visión. En esta sección, descubrirás un portafolio que fusiona la técnica impecable con un profundo sentido artístico. Cada retrato es un testimonio de la colaboración con modelos, diseñadores y estilistas, creando narrativas visuales que no solo muestran la ropa, sino la esencia y la personalidad detrás de ella. OSCAR MENDOZA Contacto +52 1 55 3228 6083 fotografooscarmendoza@gmail.com Copyright © Oscar Mendoza. Todos los derechos reservados. Aviso de privacidad

items.title: Producto
items.text: Producto Inicio Bio Clientes Contacto Inicio Bio Clientes Contacto Producto Un buen producto merece una imagen que hable por sí misma. Con una meticulosa atención al detalle y un manejo magistral de la luz, esta galería exhibe cómo la fotografía puede transformar un objeto en una pieza de deseo. Desde el lujo hasta los sabores elegancia cada fotografía está diseñada para resaltar texturas, acabados y la identidad de la marca, impulsando su valor en el mercado. OSCAR MENDOZA Contacto +52 1 55 3228 6083 fotografooscarmendoza@gmail.com Copyright © Oscar Mendoza. Todos los derechos reservados. Aviso de privacidad

items.title: Master Class y Talleres
items.text: Master Class y Talleres Inicio Bio Clientes Contacto Inicio Bio Clientes Contacto Master Class y talleres Comparto mi pasión a través del conocimiento. Mi lente no solo captura imágenes, también me permite compartir la experiencia y los saberes que hay detrás de cada proyecto. En esta sección, verás algunos testimonios visuales de mis participaciones como docente y ponente, donde he tenido el privilegio de guiar a profesionales de la fotografía y creativos para dominar el arte de la iluminación, la composición y la dirección de proyectos. ¡Cuenta con mi experiencia para tu próximo evento! Si buscas inspirar, educar y profesionalizar a tu audiencia, soy el experto que necesitas . Con mi habilidad para desglosar temas complejos en conceptos prácticos y aplicables, he impartido talleres y masterclasses sobre mis áreas de especialidad: Fotografía de retrato: La dirección artística y técnica para crear narrativas visuales impactantes. Fotografía automotriz: El arte de capturar la dinámica, el diseño y la potencia de un vehículo. Fotografía de producto: Cómo maximizar el valor de una marca a través de la imagen. OSCAR MENDOZA Contacto +52 1 55 3228 6083 fotografooscarmendoza@gmail.com Copyright © Oscar Mendoza. Todos los derechos reservados. Aviso de privacidad

items.title: 820 Ebony/Jet: Visions of the Johnson Publishing Company, an American Icon – MW Editions
items.text: 820 Ebony/Jet: Visions of the Johnson Publishing Company, an American Icon – MW Editions Skip to the content Search MW Editions MW Editions Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Search for: Close search Close Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Books 820 Ebony/Jet: Visions of the Johnson Publishing Company, an American Icon By Barbara Karant Foreword by Deborah Willis Essays by Aaron Bryant , Cheryl Finley , Carla Williams , Jon Ott , Brenna Wynn Greer , and E. James West $ 65.00 820 Ebony/Jet: Visions of the Johnson Publishing Company, an American Icon quantity Add to cart Hardcover 9.25 x 11 inches 240 pages 142 color, 8 black and white images ISBN: 978-1-969303-04-3 Description Additional information This book by photographer Barbara Karant commemorates and reflects on the Johnson Publishing Company, publisher of the iconic Ebony and Jet magazines and the most influential Black-owned media corporation of its day. Karant spent more than three years documenting the company’s historic building at 820 S. Michigan Avenue in downtown Chicago, capturing the last vestiges of the original workspace after the company sold the building in 2010 and relocated in 2012. These vibrant interiors, which remained largely unchanged from 1972 to 2012, fostered the creativity of a staff working in a variety of media. Each floor of the eleven-story building flaunted distinct color and pattern combinations, and its bold, contemporary design telegraphed JPC’s position at the forefront of Black American business and culture. When Karant photographed the vacant building, its residual textures, patterns, colors, and structures maintained the spirit of the company. Stripped of its furnishings, the interiors of the former JPC headquarters simultaneously represent the spirit of this landmark company and the sense of its loss, of a seminal moment in Black American history and the history of this nation. Accompanying the approximately 140 color photographs by Karant are essays by scholars of American art and cultural history exploring JPC’s vast influence. Documentary images of the original interiors, along with other archival material accompany the texts, which address JPC’s dominance as an image and tastemaker in mid- to late-twentieth century America, the landscape of American Black media, the Ebony in-house photo studio, and the site-specific lobby sculpture by Richard Hunt. Short texts by former employees who worked in the building contribute important documentation to JPC’s history. 820 Ebony/Jet is a tribute to the achievements of this remarkable American company. Additional information Weight 3.375 lbs Dimensions 11 × 9.25 × 1.5 in About the Author Barbara Karant is nationally recognized within the design, art, and architecture communities for her distinctive photographic vision. She is a published author, an architectural and interiors photographer, an artist, and an educator. Her work has been widely exhibited in galleries and museums throughout the United States and

items.title: Paros – MW Editions
items.text: Paros – MW Editions Skip to the content Search MW Editions MW Editions Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Search for: Close search Close Menu Books Artists Merch About Cart Books Paros By Platon $ 95.00 Edition Selection Choose an option Standard Signed Clear Paros quantity Add to cart Hardbound 12 x 12 inches 370 pages 225 black and white photographs 3 gatefolds ISBN: 9781969303081 Description Additional information In the middle of the sapphire-blue Aegean Sea lies Paros, a tiny island with an ancient history. Part of the Cycladic islands, Paros has been famous for its sparkling white marble statuary for thousands of years. Even into the early 21 st century and despite the growing influx of tourists visiting the island’s pristine beaches and charming whitewashed villages, the lifestyle on Paros remained proudly traditional. Renowned portrait photographer Platon, who traces his family roots there, has inhabited the island on and off since he was a young boy. Beginning 40 years ago, he began to capture the cadences and textures of its unique identity, which is defined by its relationship to the ocean and the sun. The black and white images in Paros show the rhythm of life—young girls in elaborate traditional dress preparing for a village festival, a weary farmer crouched in front of his grape vines to escape the beating sun, a donkey making its way up a stony path, and the proprietor of the village coffee shop taking a break, his table cluttered with a full ashtray, Greek coffee, and a glass of ouzo . The photographs reveal a place that was slow to adopt the technology and frenetic pace of life that had already overtaken much of the planet by the 1980s and 90s. An old man photographed in his kitchen sits in front of a package of AA batteries hanging on the wall behind him—the man had no idea what the batteries were for, but he assumed that they were decorative since the package had a hole in it. Paros is the most personal photography book to date by Platon, a poetic and loving tribute to a bygone world. Additional information Weight 8.5 lbs Dimensions 12 × 12 × 3 in Edition Selection Standard, Signed About the Author Platon is one of the world’s most renowned portrait photographers and has photographed more world leaders than anyone else in history, among them six American presidents. He has photographed over 30 covers for Time magazine, including Vladimir Putin for its 2008 Person of the Year cover, which was awarded first prize at the World Press Photo Contest, and Donald J. Trump for its 2024 Person of the Year cover. As staff photographer for the New Yorker , he won a Peabody Award and two National Magazine Awards. He has published four books with subjects ranging from the power of world leaders to the dignity of those who serve in the US military. Using the set pieces of a cafe, a library, a cinema, a living room, a bar, a conference facility, the lobby spaces on the Ground and Lower Floors offer building tenants places to work, meet, have coffee, get away from the upstairs hustle, to feel a generous sense of openness and productivity and to work in different ways. The design language is reduced but opulent. The design intends to combine what employees like about the “home office” and migrate that to the shared office – to have choices where you work, to work in a comfortable and relaxed way, to use domestic furniture and lighting conditions – to not feel so much like an old-fashioned “office.” The design offers office workers something more from their “shared office” than they could get from their “home office”- social interactions, a sense of being part of a team, nicer and larger scaled furniture than they have at home, settings like you’d see in a hotel lobby or a hip bar or a nice restaurant. This approach embraces the sharing economy – that you can get more than what you have in your own home by sharing it with the people you work with. The design proves that one need not use expensive materials to make a splash. A number of cost-effective strategies were used to make the effect. items.text: Bruzkus Greenberg | Live Blue Box Stuttgart Duet The Kastle The Green Box Estradenhaus Penthouse Tenerife Villa Landgut Gühlen Esters Apartment Cumberland Finnlaendische Strasse Apartment K 1.0 Wohnung GA Apartment PP Apartment MM Photographer's Loft Blue Box · info Blue Box When the clients found the rooftop apartment in Prenzlauer Berg, the thing they liked the most about it was how the wind blew over the roofs from one side of the apartment to the other when all the doors to each of the rooms were open. There were a lot of walls making a lot of small spaces that were cut off from each other. The design solution was to remove all the walls from the main space but to reinforce the sense of an inner core, around which circulation would be structured. An unused fireplace was also in the way – it sat rhetorically at the center of what felt like a stair hall that led to the roof terrace - but there was nowhere to sit near the fireplace, since everything was circulation space, and no one ever made a fire. The blue millwork box at the center of the apartment reinforces a new core, allowing light, air and space to flow around it and unify the space. This “blue box” combines wall paneling, shelving, and a built-in banquette to define the dining area and is stained - and not painted - so that the grain of the natural wood shines through. A further part of the spatial composition is another built-in box, a full-height closet/shelving unit made from a transparent finish on wood with mirrored panels that visually double the space. A light blue curtain can be hidden out of the way to open all the spaces – or can be closed to scale off the bedroom and separate it from social spaces. A bespoke butter-yellow sofa, designed specifically for the room and named “Sophia 3000” anchors the living area. The design flows from a conversation between the architecture, the built-in cabinetry, and the loose furnishings. A continuously sloping blue ceiling unites the parts and allows the space of the living room to blur with the space of the home office and bedroom. One enters from the apartment building stairway directly into the blue box, dark and relatively low, and then one emerges through the blue box into a taller, brighter room with a skylight all the way at the height of the ceiling. Sky blue stairs take you to the roof terrace, where a built-in seating area creates a cozy corner with sweeping views over Berlin. The project is a renovation of a cold and sterile rooftop apartment into a warm and sophisticated pied-à-terre with color and feeling. The transformation involved removing unnecessary walls to open up the space – and to make a new cozy interior of built-in and freestanding furniture. A blue millwork box at the center of the apartment reinforces a new core, allowing light, air and space to flow around it and to unify the space. Our design created new openings in walls and floors to create a continuous flow of space and daylight, creating an architectural promenade that linked all the parts. The main uses of the library were all given their own dedicated outdoor green courtyards - public area, city library, youth culture, and staff offices. Shortlisted finalist. Competition entry in collaboration with Baupiloten BDA. Location: Kassel Year: 2026 Team: Ester Bruzkus, Peter Greenberg, Anna Kopeina Baupiloten, Berlin Future Horizons - Alexander Tutsek Stiftung · info Future Horizons - Alexander Tutsek Stiftung The design of the exhibition to mark twenty five years of the Alexander Tutsek Foundation brings together a diverse group of works in glass in two galleries on two different floors. The works are situated in the context of “future horizons” – that is, not just as a look back, but as an anticipatory look forward. The design creates space for the encounter with an individual object while maintaining a unified sense of the overall collection. On the ground floor, works are grouped that are limited in coloration – and matte-colored display cases have been built into the walls to maintain a unified sense of the whole gallery space. The floor is left open for the display of more works. Upstairs, it is different: the works themselves have much more color – and, in contrast with the downstairs room, a shiny colorful table occupies the middle of the room, signaling the difference. On both floors, the gallery space ends with mirrored surfaces that double the visitor’s perception of the rooms. We want the visitor to gaze into the horizon and to consider these works in the flow of time, not just a look back. The mirrors in the display cases also seem to expand one’s sense of space past the walls of the gallery, playing with one’s perspective and edge definition. The reflections invite the visitor to consider the individual object in the context of simultaneously seeing the room behind them. The design attempts to resolve some of the dualities implicit in the presentation of a retrospective show of diverse works in glass - a room upstairs and a room downstairs, small studio glass pieces and large installation pieces, a narrative to describe the history of looking forward that does not look backwards. Crafted from lambskin leather and scratch-resistant glass, these over-ear headphones are built for those who appreciate both exceptional sound and elevated aesthetics. At the core of the H100 are custom 40mm titanium drivers, delivering detailed, dynamic audio with remarkable clarity and depth. Support for Dolby Atmos and Spatial Audio with dynamic head tracking creates an immersive, three-dimensional soundscape that adjusts naturally with your movement. Noise control is equally advanced. Ten integrated microphones enable precise Active Noise Cancellation and TrueTransparency™ modes, allowing seamless shifts between focused listening and ambient awareness. Intuitive haptic dials on each earcup offer effortless control over volume and sound modes. Designed for life on the move, the H100 offers up to 32 hours of battery life with ANC enabled, or 30 hours with Spatial Audio and head tracking active. A five-minute charge adds an extra five hours of playback—ideal for fast-paced schedules. The included pouch is crafted from durable cowhide leather with a soft inner lining, offering protection for both the headphones and their accessories, while adding a refined finishing touch for storage. Built with modularity in mind, the H100 features easily replaceable components—including ear pads, headbands, batteries, and circuit boards—extending the product’s lifespan and aligning with a more sustainable approach to design. items.text: On The Move: The M4 MacBook Air | Softer Volumes On The Move: The M4 MacBook Air | Softer Volumes Softer Volumes On The Move: The M4 MacBook Air Work, study, or create wherever you are The new Macbook Air from Apple boasts no shortage of features; alongside the new Sky Blue colourway, it also features an M4 chip for fast performance even under the most intensive workloads, up to 18 hours of battery life, and a vibrant Liquid Retina display that renders text and images clearly and brilliantly, all for a lower starting price than the previous generation. The extended battery life and thin, portable design—crafted from hard-wearing yet lightweight aluminium—make the M4 MacBook Air perfect for those who work, study, or create on the move. The 13” model optimises portability while the 15” model strikes a balance between size, weight, and screen space. For those with a dedicated workspace who need to handle more diverse tasks, both models support up to two external displays. Both models also benefit from a fanless design, making the MacBook Air thinner—and quieter—than ever. At less than half an inch in thickness, this generation of Airs is incredibly sleek, and the new Sky Blue colour only further establishes Apple’s streamlined aesthetic. Consuming content and taking part in video and audio calls is enhanced by the Macbook Air’s finely-tuned sound system—with support for Spatial Audio and Dolby Atmos—plus a three-mic array for improved clarity and the 12MP Center Stage camera, which keeps you in the centre of the frame during calls and allows you to share a top-down view of your desk in Desk View. And, with macOS Sequoia, built-in Apple Intelligence helps optimise your workflow, offering tools that help elevate your writing, photos, and videos. With a host of internal and external improvements, this is truly a laptop designed to enhance your life and work wherever you are, whether it’s home, the office, or somewhere further afield. apple.com Words by Rowan Trehane Photographs by Joe Vuong This article was produced by Softer Volumes in partnership with Apple. items.title: Fusion of Futuristic and Earthy Design at Dome Restaurant in Bali | Softer Volumes
items.text: Fusion of Futuristic and Earthy Design at Dome Restaurant in Bali | Softer Volumes Fusion of Futuristic and Earthy Design at Dome Restaurant in Bali | Softer Volumes Softer Volumes A Harmonious Fusion of Futuristic and Earthy Design Inside Dome, a New Restaurant at Bali’s Desa Potato Head Desa Potato Head in Bali, known for its blend of cultural experiences and sustainability, introduces Dome—a culinary concept that merges futuristic design with eco-conscious aesthetics. This latest addition not only brings a unique approach dining but also emphasises community and creativity. Dome’s interior draws inspiration from Buckminster Fuller’s Dome Home, encapsulating a retro-futuristic ambiance within the striking architecture designed by OMA. The space features a central circular bar surrounded by stainless steel monoliths housing iconic JBL 4355 speakers, creating a high-tech yet earthy feel. Complementing these elements are Indonesian tribal sculptures, like those of the Asmat, adding an authentic cultural touch. Dome prioritises sustainability, utilising reclaimed wood and furniture throughout the space. Antique rugs add a homey feel, while staff uniforms are crafted from upcycled cotton. This approach not only reduces waste but also celebrates the beauty of imperfections, as highlighted by Creative Director Isaac Larose: “If you look closely, you can see the imperfections in the shades of the reclaimed furniture. We decided to celebrate these imperfections rather than hide them, just like we do with our wines and produce.” Designed as a place for connection, Dome features a large communal area where guests can mingle and draw inspiration from a curated selection of books on architecture, design, art, food, and wellness. Custom-designed pieces, including OMA-designed sofas and lounge chairs by Potato Head’s in-house design studio, enhance the inviting atmosphere. Chef Diego Recarte’s menu at Dome offers a modern take on food, inspired by his experiences in South American and European kitchens. The dishes highlight locally sourced ingredients from organic farmers, while the wine bar features natural, organic, and biodynamic options. This commitment to conscious consumption aligns with Desa Potato Head’s broader philosophy of ‘Good Times, Do Good.’ seminyak.potatohead.co Words by Hugo Johnson Photographs supplied by Potato Head Softer Volumes: Cafés — Digital Book 290 beautifully-designed cafés around the world, showcased in a premium digital book. items.text: Alor Design Studio: Community and Sustainability Driven Design | Softer Volumes Alor Design Studio: Community and Sustainability Driven Design | Softer Volumes Softer Volumes Community and Sustainability Driven Design Alor Design Studio Newly-launched Alor Design Studio takes a refreshing approach to furniture design, firmly rooted in the belief that thoughtfully designed, skilfully handcrafted and sustainable furniture should be accessible to everyone. Their collection is also a celebration of Australian design, created in collaboration with both established and emerging local designers, resulting in unique pieces that reflect Alor’s commitment to community engagement. By working closely with local creatives, Alor aims to push the limits of Australian furniture design, building and nurturing a community that values design excellence and collective creativity, and crafting pieces that reflect a shared vision of innovation. Through this approach, Alor also provides a platform on which to showcase local talent and help develop creative careers. The brand’s first collaboration is with Melbourne-based industrial designer, James Walsh. Together Walsh and Alor Design Studio have created the Assemble Range—a collection centred around the idea of bringing people together, designed to showcase natural materials and considered craftsmanship. The range—built from FSC-certified timbers sourced from sustainable forestries, like all Alor furniture—features clean lines, soft curves and elegant joinery. Sustainability, to which Alor takes a holistic approach, lies at the very heart of the brand’s philosophy, and informs the design process from the ground up. Alor’s furniture is made to last, both in the timelessness of its design and in its solid construction. Each product is made with carefully-sourced materials—chosen for quality and sustainable production—and durable hardware, and designed with replaceable components where possible to ensure longevity. Combined with subtly playful designs, Alor’s collections form a legacy of Australian design to be used and treasured now and by generations to come. Alor will be showcasing its collection at the Decor and Design Show from 17th–19th July 2024 at the Melbourne Exhibition Centre. This offers visitors a chance to experience Alor’s products firsthand for the first time, and further explore the brand’s commitment to sustainability, craft and community. alor.studio Words by Rowan Trehane Photographs by Matt Mcquiggan Softer Volumes: Cafés — Digital Book 290 beautifully-designed cafés around the world, showcased in a premium digital book. W1T 6AJ T +44(0)20 7436 8846 Hong Kong Ground Floor 12 Kennedy Street Wan Chai Hong Kong T +852 2804 1138 Mandarin Oriental The Landmark, Hong Kong More than a decade after reimagining the hotel, Joyce Wang Studio returns to renovate the guestrooms, spa and public spaces of Mandarin Oriental The Landmark, Hong Kong. Located in the heart of Central, the hotel offers a retreat from one of the city’s densely built districts. The design draws inspiration from the historic mansion houses of Hong Kong’s New Territories, once frequented by the Tai Kwuns of a bygone era. Through a carefully curated blend of architecture, art, and materiality, the hotel is envisioned as a contemporary pied-à-terre, offering guests an intimate connection to Hong Kong’s cultural heritage, and layered sense of place. Stepping in from the bustle of Central, guests are welcomed into a dramatic double-height space where a rich palette of stone, timber, textured wallcoverings, and custom églomisé glass creates an immediate sense of calm. A sculptural Irish pewter staircase rises through the foyer, complemented by warm red stone accents and curated artwork that evoke the experience of arriving at a grand, storied residence. The reception, concierge, and lounge spaces are conceived as a contemporary interpretation of a lived-in mansion. Sculptural plinths, artwork niches, and carefully curated objects create moments of pause throughout the guest journey, while bespoke furnishings and layered materials lend a sense of warmth and familiarity. Inspired by the character of historic Hong Kong residences, the spaces balance the grandeur of arrival with the intimacy of home. Located just off the reception lounge, Communal reimagines the hotel’s iconic MO Bar as an all-day gathering space led by Michelin-starred Chef Richard Ekkebus . Inspired by the spirit of a family living room within a grand mansion, the design combines patinated brass, verdigris and bronze finishes with fluted jade-toned tiles and warm tangerine upholstery, creating a welcoming setting that transitions seamlessly from morning espresso to evening cocktails. The renovation encompassed the hotel’s L450, L600 and L900 suites, alongside its guestrooms, creating a refreshed residential experience rooted in Hong Kong’s architectural heritage. In collaboration with Fromental, Joyce Wang Studio developed a bespoke wallcovering inspired by reflections captured in the windows of historic mansion houses and the weathered textures of their façades. items.text: Genso | Joyce Wang Studio scrollTop: 0px, scrollLeft: 0px --> Skip to content Design Bespoke Design Bespoke --> DJA --> About Contact En Menu --> --> Design Bespoke About Contact En En Cn --> Enquiries General info@joycewangstudio.com New Business info@joycewangstudio.com Press laura@lbagency.co Jobs apply@joycewangstudio.com London 1 Warren Mews London. W1T 6AJ T +44(0)20 7436 8846 Hong Kong Ground Floor 12 Kennedy Street Wan Chai Hong Kong T +852 2804 1138 Genso, Sha Tin Racecourse, Hong Kong Genso, a spirited dining and entertainment destination at the Hong Kong Jockey Club’s Sha Tin Racecourse, designed to immerse guests in the vibrant world of horse racing culture. Conceived as a retro fantasy land, Genso comes alive with a bold, eccentric-urban aesthetic – fusing culinary creativity, live racing energy, and playful nostalgia to attract a new generation of racing enthusiasts. Play Pause Sound: on Sound: off Set across two distinctive floors, the space invites guests on a layered, experiential journey. On the lower floor, the Fudo Town Food Hall captures the animated atmosphere of a market, serving the best of Japanese street food in a lively, casual setting. As guests ascend to the upper level, the experience enters a more refined realm at Izakaya, where a dramatic suspended walkway of neon-clad floating islands connect pockets of intimate dining poised above the action below. Rooted in the iconic streetscapes of Tokyo’s Golden Gai, the electric neon of Blade Runner, and the dynamism of manga; the studio’s design reimagines the racecourse as a cinematic cityscape. A hive of activity, the space evokes an intrinsic feeling of adventure and discovery in its guests, as they explore the eclectic food and drink offerings and arcade-style activities, while offering ever-changing perspectives of the horse racing below. The space is brought to life by a dizzying dream-like palette of teal and aqua, set alongside bold orange and peach tones. Warm timber finishes, bold patterned upholstery and mid-century geometric details define the scheme, while dramatic ceilings are enhanced by a rhythmic array of lanterns and the neon floating islands, referencing the graphic nature of neon street signage. Intricate ceramic tiles wrapping the columns allude to building facades, further shaping the immersive aesthetic of the cityscape. items.title: Approach - Studio Dado
items.text: Approach - Studio Dado Studio DADO Menu Close Projects Approach About Us News Blog Contact Navigate Projects Approach About Us News Blog Contact [email protected] 786.433.2500 Approach Working with us is a true creative partnership. Our clients understand what their spaces need to feel like, and to uncover that, we take the time to truly understand every nuance. Explore Our Approach Each project begins with how the space should feel, shaped by the client’s vision, the energy they want to create, and the moments they hope to inspire. Design for the human experience. Every element we design begins with empathy. We think about how a guest will enter a space, what they’ll notice first, and what small comforts will shape their experience. From the soft glow of morning light to the natural rhythm of a room’s layout, even down to the velvet lining of a drawer, our work reflects a deep care for how people feel—physically and emotionally—within a space. No two stories are the same, and neither are the spaces that hold them. Each design takes shape through the details: the function it must serve, the room it has to breathe, the people behind it, and the ideas that inspire it. We immerse ourselves in those particulars to build layered, unforgettable environments where meaning lives in every corner. At the heart of our design philosophy is the belief that true luxury is multisensory, a delicate dance between what you see, feel, and intuitively move through. Every element has been considered: the way a corridor curves, the softness of a chair beneath your hand, the gentle glow of ambient lighting that shifts with the time of day. Our design choices are not simply aesthetic; they are emotional. We design with the spirit in mind, to uplift, to calm, to spark curiosity, and to create moments of stillness or awe. Our spaces are meant to be lived in and deeply felt. Let’s work together Empathy, embedded Let’s work together We bring together beauty and utility to create spaces that resonate on a human level. When design feels personal, the connection becomes unforgettable. As true partners, we stay connected, supporting our clients beyond the final reveal. Our Projects Let’s work together Because good food always tastes better in a well-designed place. A place to sleep, perchance to dream. Places to unwind, connect with friends and maybe meet someone new. The spaces in between the spaces, where life's rich pageant unfolds and the beauty of design reveals itself. These spaces take you to your happy place, where every detail is intentional and considered.
